newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB barley monopoly voter response very good - KPMG.
newsitem.headline: CWB barley monopoly voter response very good - KPMG.

text.p: The number of returned mail-in ballots on whether the Canadian Wheat Board should retain its monopoly on feed and malt barley exports surpassed the 50 percent mark Wednesday, consultant firm KPMG said.

"To date we've received 43,000 ballots. That represents more than 50 percent of eligible voters. It's a very good response rate, we're actually quite pleased with it. We're expecting additional thousands between now and the close of the vote," KPMG associate Joanne Pindera told Reuters.
About 76,000 Prairie farmers were asked whether they want to retain the status quo or export barley via private firms.
The voter response rate reached 56.6 percent Wednesday.
About 30 percent of barley grown on the Prairies is exported and the balace is fed to livestock or brewed in Canada.
Western Canada produced about 15 million tonnes of barley in 1996, private and Statistics Canada estimates show.
Ballots post-marked after February 28 will not be enumerated, Pindera said.
